newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb posts fourth-quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb posts fourth-quarter profit.

text.p: Eye care power Bausch & Lomb Inc. on Wednesday reported a fourth-quarter profit that followed a loss in the same period a year ago, and announced it would cut 175 jobs in the United States and Europe.

The Rochester, N.Y.-based maker of contact lenses, sunglasses and other products posted net income of $15.8 million, or 29 cents a share, compared with a loss of $3.4 million, or 4 cents a share, in last year's fourth quarter.
Bausch & Lomb rang up $434.8 million in net sales in the fourth quarter, down 4 percent from $455.1 million in the year-ago period.
The company said it suffered a 21 percent decline in revenues from its eyewear segment, primarily due to the cancellation of orders by its largest sunglass customer, Sunglass Hut International Inc.

Bausch & Lomb noted that restructuring charges reduced earnings by $17.4 million in 1995's fourth quarter and that the sale of its Steri-Oss unit increased its 1996 fourth-quarter net income by $8.5 million.

The 175 job cuts in the United States and Europe will occur primarily in Bausch & Lomb's corporate staff, vision care and pharmaceutical divisions and are part of the company's continuing streamlining effort, it said. Bausch & Lomb employs more than 13,000 people in 35 countries.

"Our goal is to establish systems and processes that are not only more efficient, but also more responsive to the rapid changes occurring in the markets in which we compete," Chief Executive William Carpenter said in a statement.

For the year, Bausch & Lomb earned $83 million, or $1.47 per share, vs. $112 million, or $1.94 per share, in 1995. Sales totalled $1.926 billion in 1996, compared with $1.932 billion in the previous year.
The company's stock dipped 12.5 cents to $32.875 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
